This sets a ceiling, not a target. Eclipse still works out how much this particular page can carry — it just will not go above what you pick here. Setting an exact number of words would not work, because how many a page can carry depends on how many of them you happen to know.

google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite was chosen by measurement: fastest, ten to thirty times cheaper than the alternatives, and it applied the most swaps. Reasoning models are a poor fit here — Eclipse has already decided every word, so thinking about it is wasted time and money.

Where your page text goes. When Eclipse is switched on for a site, the sentences on screen are sent to Hack Club AI to be rewritten. Eclipse is off on every site until you switch it on, and it refuses to run at all on banking, email, health and sign-in pages. That refusal cannot be turned off.
